text.p: St Petersburg City Telephone (PTS) revenues should surge with the introduction of local call charges and is a good conservative buy with relatively high liquidity, CentreInvest Group said.
The Moscow brokerage said shares could rise to about $1.67. PTS traded at $1.45 in early trading on Tuesday on the Russian Trading System.
It said in a new report that local call charges, planned for introduction in the first half of 1997, would spur fast revenue growth for PTS, Russia's second largest local telecoms firm.
But the plan could be delayed by the city government which opposes metering until 1998, delaying growth as well.

CentreInvest said PTS was generally overvalued compared to other Russian regional telecoms companies but that strong first half 1996 revenue -- 79 percent up year-on-year -- suggested some revaluation was in order.
It also said the company was cheap compared to foreign telecoms, with a market capitalisation/lines in service ratio of $303.16 compared to $1,181.36 for Thai Telephone and Telecommunications.
